axes.decision: Analysis sample within each form file / missing-data handling

levels.description: Keep all records in the form file; item statistics on available cases per item; CFA and invariance models on cases complete on the 19 retained items (listwise, PRELIS/LISREL default).
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: Article reports one n per form and year and says nothing about missing data; listwise deletion is the LISREL 8.7 default when a raw data file is read.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10 Method; p. 10 Preliminary Analyses (LISREL 8.7)

levels.description: Listwise deletion on all 23 Form 4 items (or all 6 Form 3 items) for every output, including item statistics.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Equally compatible with the single reported n per form; changes item-level n and possibly means.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10

levels.description: Full-information maximum likelihood for the CFA/invariance models using all cases with at least one valid item.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Available in LISREL 8.7; not described; expected to give similar latent means when missingness is low.
levels.source_locator: Enders, C. K., & Bandalos, D. L. (2001). The relative performance of FIML estimation for missing data in SEM. Structural Equation Modeling, 8, 430-457.

axes.decision: Use of the survey sampling weight

levels.description: Unweighted.
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: No weighting statement anywhere in the article; LISREL analyses described without weights.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF pp. 9-10 Method; pp. 14-15 Primary Analyses

levels.description: Weight all descriptive statistics, t tests (weighted means/SDs with nominal n) and the CFA covariance matrices by V5.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Provider recommends V5 for all analyses; public weights are bracketed; effect on means expected small but not established in the article.
levels.source_locator: sources/source_description.md Weights; Kish, L. (1965). Survey sampling. Wiley. (use of design weights for descriptive population estimates)

axes.decision: Denominator of d for latent mean differences

levels.description: sqrt((SD_earlier^2 + SD_later^2)/2): equal-weight pooled SD of the two groups.
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: Formula not stated; this is the standard Cohen d and is the pooled form consistent with the published-record forensic check (forensics.json F01).
levels.source_locator: Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical power analysis for the behavioral sciences (2nd ed.). Erlbaum. (d with pooled SD; article cites the 1977 edition); P1 PDF p. 15 'Cohen, 1977'

levels.description: df-weighted pooled SD sqrt(((n1-1)SD1^2+(n2-1)SD2^2)/(n1+n2-2)).
levels.label: equivalent
levels.rationale: With group sizes of similar magnitude the two pooled forms differ negligibly.
levels.source_locator: Hedges, L. V., & Olkin, I. (1985). Statistical methods for meta-analysis. Academic Press. (pooled SD weighted by df; small-sample correction g)

levels.description: Hedges' g small-sample correction applied to L0 or L1.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.rationale: Correction factor is essentially 1 for thousands of cases per group.
levels.source_locator: Hedges, L. V., & Olkin, I. (1985). Statistical methods for meta-analysis. Academic Press. (pooled SD weighted by df; small-sample correction g)

levels.description: SD of the earlier (reference) year only (Glass's delta).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Plausible for a 'baseline' framing (Figure 1 uses the earliest year as zero baseline) but not described; differs when SDs change across years.
levels.source_locator: Glass, G. V., McGaw, B., & Smith, M. L. (1981). Meta-analysis in social research. Sage. (control-group SD standardizer); P1 PDF p. 16 Figure 1 note

axes.decision: Which SD accompanies the latent means (standardizer for d)

levels.description: Model-implied latent SD per group = sqrt(factor variance) under the Model 4 solution with the metric of AX05.
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: Table 1 note says the scale rows report latent means; SDs printed under them are most naturally the latent SDs on the same metric; article does not define them.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 13 Table 1 note; Hancock, G. R. (2001). Effect size, power, and sample size determination for structured means modeling and MIMIC approaches. Psychometrika, 66, 373-388. (latent d standardized by latent SD)

levels.description: Observed SD of the unit-weighted mean of the scale items per group (available cases).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Equally compatible with the table layout (item rows print observed SDs); yields a different standardizer and hence different d.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF pp. 11-13 Table 1 layout

axes.decision: Identification and scaling of latent means in the multigroup model

levels.description: Marker-variable identification: first-listed item of each factor has loading fixed to 1 and intercept fixed to 0 in every group; latent means free in all groups (latent means on the marker item's metric).
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: Latent means are reported for all three groups on the item response metric, which requires a marker/intercept scaling rather than a reference-group zero; the first-listed items are not footnoted as freed intercepts, consistent with their use as markers (observation, not stated).
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF pp. 11-13 Table 1; p. 13 footnote a

levels.description: Reference-group identification: earliest-year latent means fixed to 0 and variances to 1; later-group means and variances free; d computed from latent mean differences and latent SDs.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Standard in Vandenberg & Lance sequence; gives the same mean differences as L0 up to the loading scale but the printed per-group means could not be produced directly.
levels.source_locator: Vandenberg, R. J., & Lance, C. E. (2000). A review and synthesis of the measurement invariance literature. Organizational Research Methods, 3, 4-70.

levels.description: Effects-coding identification (loadings average 1, intercepts sum to 0 per factor).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Produces latent means on the average-item metric; plausible given latent means lie near item means, but not described.
levels.source_locator: Little, T. D., Slegers, D. W., & Card, N. A. (2006). A non-arbitrary method of identifying and scaling latent variables in SEM. Structural Equation Modeling, 13, 59-72.

levels.description: Normal-theory maximum likelihood on Pearson covariance matrices and means (LISREL 8.7 default).
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: LISREL 8.7 named; no estimator stated; ML chi-square differences reported without scaling.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10 Preliminary Analyses; p. 14 Table 2

levels.description: ML point estimates with Satorra-Bentler scaled chi-square/robust SEs.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Same latent means and d; alters fit statistics and SEs used for the CIs and invariance decisions.
levels.source_locator: Satorra, A., & Bentler, P. M. (2001). A scaled difference chi-square test statistic. Psychometrika, 66, 507-514.

levels.description: Ordinal estimation (polychoric correlations, WLS/DWLS).
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.rationale: Changes the latent metric (thresholds instead of intercepts), so latent means and d are not comparable to the reported item-metric means.
levels.source_locator: Flora, D. B., & Curran, P. J. (2004). An empirical evaluation of alternative methods of estimation for CFA with ordinal data. Psychological Methods, 9, 466-491.

levels.description: Student independent-samples t with pooled variance, two-sided, item-level available n.
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: Only 't' is stated; pooled t is the conventional default.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 13 Table 1 header 't or d'

levels.description: Welch unequal-variance t.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.rationale: With thousands of cases per group and similar SDs, t values are practically identical.
levels.source_locator: Welch, B. L. (1947). The generalization of 'Student's' problem when several different population variances are involved. Biometrika, 34, 28-35.

levels.description: Design-weighted t (V5) with nominal n.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Follows AX02.L1; not described.
levels.source_locator: sources/source_description.md Weights

axes.decision: Assignment of the four dropped Form 4 items to the security and influence factors in the seven-factor diagnostic model

levels.description: security = {secure future, establish roots}; influence = {participate in decision making, difficult and challenging problems}.
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: Follows item content and the cited prior factor structure (Johnson, 2000); not stated item by item.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10 Preliminary Analyses (Johnson, 2000); p. 13 Table 1 'Omitted items'

levels.description: Any other partition of the four items into two two-item factors.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Not determinable from the article; affects only the seven-factor fit and alphas, not the focal comparisons.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10

axes.decision: Which five Form 3 items form the 'work centrality' factor and which is the single 'job stability' indicator

levels.description: Stability indicator = 'stay in the same job for most of my adult life' (V028); centrality = the other four agreement items plus the yes/no enough-money item (V024-V027, V029).
levels.label: origin
levels.rationale: The article calls the single item a question about job stability, which matches V028's wording; the yes/no item is explicitly listed among the Form 3 questions.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10 Method; p. 13 Table 1 'Omitted items' order

levels.description: Centrality = the five agreement items V024-V028; the yes/no item V029 excluded from the CFA.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.rationale: Also consistent with 'five questions ... on a 5-point scale'; diagnostic only.
levels.source_locator: P1 PDF p. 10

notes: Alternatives need an article or methodological-literature basis. Explicitly reported items/controls cannot be changed within the equivalent set. Distinct reported outcomes are not interchangeable specifications. Fixed (not open): the 19-item five-factor item assignment; the six freed intercepts; the three survey years and two forms; the sign convention later minus earlier; the top-category percentage definitions; the .002 delta-CFI criterion.
